quiz.q: In Rajni Kothari's analysis of the 'Congress system', what role did opposition parties play?
options: They operated from the margins as parties of pressure rather than viable alternatives to govern.
They formed durable ideological coalitions to regularly alternate power with Congress at the national level.
They acted as the primary agenda-setters while Congress merely implemented consensus policies from the centre.
They functioned as anti-system revolutionary groups seeking to dismantle the constitutional framework of representative democracy.
quiz.why: Rajni Kothari characterized Congress as a party of consensus, while peripheral opposition parties acted as parties of pressure influencing decisions from the margins.

quiz.q: According to the class notes, what was the primary internal cause of Congress fragmentation and regional party formation?
options: The frequent conduct of competitive intra-party elections that deepened irreconcilable factional rivalries across state units.
The excessive centralization of power in the high command that drove regional leaders to exit.
The complete transformation of the party into an ideologically rigid organisation staffed exclusively by cadres.
The constitutional amendments that formally barred national political parties from contesting legislative elections in states.
quiz.why: The deinstitutionalisation of democracy and centralisation of power under the central leadership forced regional satraps to leave and launch regional parties.

quiz.q: How does Professor Vidyut Chakrabarty contrast Indian coalition politics with Western coalition governance?
options: Indian coalitions are built upon shared ideological principles rather than pragmatic electoral calculations.
Western coalitions rely on oversized partnerships because coalition partners frequently threaten to defect.
Indian coalitions are tactical calculations formed primarily as negative alliances to block rivals.
Western coalitions operate as ad hoc partnerships that continuously search for institutional design.
quiz.why: Unlike Western coalitions designed around ideological coherence to govern, Indian coalitions are tactical calculations formed to keep opponents out of power.

quiz.q: Why do the lecture notes reject switching to a presidential system to resolve coalition instability in India?
options: A presidential executive requires a two-party system that is explicitly prohibited by the Indian Constitution.
The Supreme Court has ruled that coalition governance is an unalterable feature of the republic.
Adopting a presidential model requires prior implementation of the German constructive vote of no confidence.
Parliamentary democracy is part of basic structure and presidentialism rarely endures outside the United States.
quiz.why: The parliamentary system is part of the basic structure of the Constitution, and presidential democracy has rarely proved stable outside the United States.
